prompt: A 1 TB SSD is rated for 0.3 drive writes per day over five years, using 365 days per year. What host-write rating does that imply?

options.explanation: The rating is 1 × 0.3 × 365 × 5 = 547.5 TB of host writes.
This omits the number of days per year.
That is only one year of the modeled rating.

options.text: 547.5 TB divided by internal write amplification
options.explanation: A host-TBW rating already measures host writes; do not divide it by internal amplification again.

workedExample:
The rating counts host writes over the specified warranty period.

```formula
W = 365 C d Y
W = 1 TB × 0.3 × 365 × 5
W = 547.5 TB
where
W: modeled total host writes in terabytes (TB)
C: drive capacity, here 1 TB
d: drive writes per day, here 0.3
Y: warranty years, here 5
365: days counted per year in this model
TB: terabyte, one trillion bytes
In words: thirty percent of the drive each day for five modeled years is 547.5 terabytes of host writes.
```

This is a workload-dependent warranty rating, not an exact failure threshold.
